questions.problem:
Calculate the minor of the entry ${x}_{21}$ in the matrix
$X=[\begin{aligned}9 & -3 & 0 \\ -2 & 8 & 6 \\ -1 & 0 & 11\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
The minor of ${x}_{21}=-2$ (second row, first column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $-2$ are removed: 

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}∗ & -3 & 0 \\ -2 & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & 0 & 11\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of ${x}_{21}=-2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & 11\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3\cdot 11-0\cdot 0 \\  & =-33-0 \\  & =-33.\end{aligned}
$$

$P=[\begin{aligned}-11 & 7 & -9 \\ 2 & -2 & 9 \\ 8 & -5 & 72\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
The minor of ${p}_{31}=8$ (third row, first column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $8$ are removed: 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}∗ & 7 & -9 \\ ∗ & -2 & 9 \\ 8 & ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of ${p}_{31}=8$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}7 & -9 \\ -2 & 9\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}7 & -9 \\ -2 & 9\end{aligned}| \\  & =7\cdot 9-(-9)\cdot (-2) \\  & =63-18 \\  & =45.\end{aligned}
$$

$Y=[\begin{aligned}15 & 8 & 9 \\ 7 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
The minor of ${y}_{13}=9$ (first row, third column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $9$ are removed: 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & 9 \\ 7 & 1 & ∗ \\ 0 & -1 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of ${y}_{13}=9$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}7 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}7 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =7\cdot (-1)-1\cdot 0 \\  & =-7-0 \\  & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

${M}_{23}=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & x & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & 4 \\ 1 & 2y & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of ${p}_{23}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{23} & =det[\begin{aligned}2 & x \\ 1 & 2y\end{aligned}] \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & x \\ 1 & 2y\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (2y)-x\cdot 1 \\  & =4y-x.\end{aligned}

$$

questions.problem:
What is the minor of ${t}_{22}$ in the matrix
$T=[\begin{aligned}3p & r & 3p \\ q & r & -q \\ -6q & -p & 6q\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and the second column:

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3p & ∗ & 3p \\ ∗ & r & ∗ \\ -6q & ∗ & 6q\end{aligned}]
$$

 

Next, we calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}3p & 3p \\ -6q & 6q\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}3p & 3p \\ -6q & 6q\end{aligned}| \\  & =3p\cdot 6q-3p\cdot (-6q) \\  & =18pq+18pq \\  & =36pq\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the minor of ${p}_{23}$ is ${t}^{2}+12$, find all the possible values of $t$ in the matrix

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}t & -8 & 3 \\ -7 & 4 & 4 \\ -1 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and third column:

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}t & -8 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & 4 \\ -1 & 9 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${p}_{23}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}t & -8 \\ -1 & 9\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}t & -8 \\ -1 & 9\end{aligned}| \\  & =t\cdot 9-(-8)\cdot (-1) \\  & =9t-8.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${p}_{23}$ is ${t}^{2}+12$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}9t-8 & ={t}^{2}+12 \\ {t}^{2}-9t+20 & =0 \\ (t-5)(t-4) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $t=4$ and $t=5.$

questions.problem:
Given that the minor of ${p}_{11}$ is $4$, find all the possible values of $t$ in the matrix

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-5t & 18 & 6t \\ -3 & 9 & 5 \\ 19t & 1 & 3t\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we remove the first row and first column:

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}5t & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & 9 & 5 \\ ∗ & 1 & 3t\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${p}_{11}$ is

 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}9 & 5 \\ 1 & 3t\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}9 & 5 \\ 1 & 3t\end{aligned}| \\  & =9\cdot 3t-5\cdot 1 \\  & =27t-5.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${p}_{11}$ is $4$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}27t-5 & =4 \\ 27t & =9 \\ t & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $t=\frac{1}{3}.$

questions.problem:
Given that the minor of ${a}_{22}$ is $-70$, find all the possible values of $k$ in the matrix

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2k & -8 & 6 \\ 0 & 5 & -7 \\ 11 & 9 & k+3\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and second column:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2k & ∗ & 6 \\ ∗ & 5 & ∗ \\ 11 & ∗ & k+3\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${a}_{22}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}2k & 6 \\ 11 & k+3\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}2k & 6 \\ 11 & k+3\end{aligned}| \\  & =2k\cdot (k+3)-11\cdot 6 \\  & =2{k}^{2}+6k-66.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${a}_{22}$ is $-70$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{k}^{2}+6k-66 & =-70 \\ 2{k}^{2}+6k+4 & =0 \\ {k}^{2}+3k+2 & =0 \\ (k+1)(k+2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $k=-1$ and $k=-2.$

questions.problem:
Given that the minor of ${b}_{33}$ is $3$, find all the possible values of $x$ in the matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}6 & -{x}^{2} & -10 \\ -5 & 8 & 1 \\ 2 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we remove the third row and third column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}6 & -{x}^{2} & ∗ \\ -5 & 8 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${b}_{33}$ is

 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}6 & -{x}^{2} \\ -5 & 8\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}6 & -{x}^{2} \\ -5 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =6\cdot 8-(-5)\cdot (-{x}^{2}) \\  & =48-5{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${b}_{33}$ is $3$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}48-5{x}^{2} & =3 \\ 45-5{x}^{2} & =0 \\ 9-{x}^{2} & =0 \\ (3-x)(3+x) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=-3$ and $x=3.$
